title: Fit neighborhood price means inside each fold
summary: Compare a global training log-price mean with one fixed neighborhood smoothing change on identical random folds. The original generated homes are separate from Ames competition data.
environment: Recorded with Python 3.12.14 and its standard library only on Darwin arm64. This local CPU run is the recorded environment; other environments are not covered by this receipt.
steps: Download and run the script with Python3.12.14. The default generated fixture needs no packages or account.
Compare the global log-price mean with the neighborhood mean smoothed using five pseudo-examples from the training global mean. Fit both inside the same five training folds.
Inspect each fold and explain errors on unseen neighborhoods. Keep the smoothing weight fixed during this experiment.
Optional: --csv authorized-train.csv reads Id,Neighborhood,SalePrice with finite positive prices. This mode is tested on generated rows; Ames competition data has not been executed.
limitations: Generated homes are not Ames competition data; no submission or historical reproduction.
Random folds do not establish spatial or temporal transfer; the neighborhood smoothing weight was fixed before evaluation.
Aggregate is mean fold log-RMSE, rather than pooled test RMSE or a competition score.
Memory measures traced Python allocations, not process RSS.
split_definition: Five shuffled random folds with seed 17; each row validates once; all log-price category means fit training rows only.
